options.content:
**Subject** is `llm/gemini.py` — the production client: Python, asyncio, one shared httpx pool, subject to the GIL. **Control** is k6 — Go, no GIL, independent connection handling, open-loop by construction.

Both hit the same endpoint with the same workload. If the subject plateaus while the control keeps climbing, the ceiling is **our client**. If both knee at the same arrival rate, the ceiling is **Vertex**. A single harness cannot distinguish those two cases, which is the entire reason the control exists.

panels.title: Throughput: subject vs control
panels.description: Divergence here is the cost of the Python client.

panels.title: p99 latency: subject vs control
panels.description: The control is open-loop, so its latency does not benefit from coordinated omission. A subject p99 that looks better than the control's is a warning sign, not a win.

panels.title: Client-side constraint signals (subject only)
panels.description: Pool saturation and event-loop lag both climbing while the control stays flat is conclusive evidence the bottleneck is ours.

panels.title: Generator health (control only)
panels.description: k6 dropped_iterations must stay at zero. Anything above zero means the generator could not sustain the offered rate, and the control is no longer a valid reference.

panels.title: Rate limiting seen by each harness
panels.description: If only one harness sees 429s at the same offered rate, quota is being attributed to something other than raw request count.
